flaws.title: Unbounded bitmap scan in downward reset ignores endTick, making zero-for-one top-of-block swaps run out of gas
flaws.sequence:
1. A pool has tickSpacing 1 (or another small spacing), and its only initialized tick below the current price is far away. This can be a full-range position whose lower tick is near MIN_TICK, or there can be no initialized tick below the price at all, for example when every position sits above the price.
2. A user makes the top-of-block zero-for-one swap with a non-zero priority fee. It moves the price down by only a few ticks.
3. afterSwap calls _zeroForOneDistributeTax, which calls initDown, which calls reset.
4. reset never compares the scanned wordPos with endTick's word. It makes one external getPoolBitmapInfo call per word until it finds any initialized bit or reaches int16.min. For a full-range position at tick 0 with spacing 1, that is about 3,466 cold external reads. With no tick below, it is about 32,768 reads, which is tens of millions to over 100M gas.
5. _zeroForOneDistributeTax then calls ticks.reset again, which doubles the cost.
6. The swap runs out of gas or hits the block gas limit and reverts.
flaws.impact: Top-of-block zero-for-one swaps become very expensive or impossible in pools with sparse or absent initialized ticks below the price. Users are denied swaps, and the MEV tax distribution path is blocked. The scan should stop once wordPos goes below the word that contains endTick.

requirement_breaks: reset does not limit its search to the [endTick, startTick] range. It reads bitmap words far past the word containing endTick, down to int16.min, instead of leaving it to the bounded _advanceToNextDown helper to stop at endTick.
